title: Back pain and anxiety, near the line
summary: Former warehouse operative with lumbar degenerative disc disease, left sciatica and generalised anxiety. Draft reaches 18 points only by combining three 6-point descriptors (1(d), 2(c), 14(c)); each is contestable, and losing any one leaves 12, so the case tests whether the AI can weigh physical and mental evidence together, resolve a UC50/physio conflict on sitting tolerance, and handle good-day/bad-day variability without overclaiming. No Schedule 7 descriptor or Schedule 8/9 circumstance is made out.
exercises: conflict: claimant's UC50 vs physio on sitting tolerance
majority of the time: good days vs bad days on mobilising
objective test result (6-minute walk test) vs self-report
cause condition: physical vs mental cause for activity 13 (reg 39(4))
unfamiliar place reached alone defeats activity 15

conditions_in_documents: Lumbar degenerative disc disease L4/5 and L5/S1

must_find.quote: Total distance 240 metres. One rest stop, standing, at approximately 170 metres, reporting left leg pain 7/10.
I can walk about 100 yards and then I have to stop and lean on something till the leg settles.
Has to stop at the bus shelter halfway on the way back "nearly every time".
says "maybe three bad days a week" when he does not go out at all except to the garden.
Client says that was "a good day, I'd taken extra tablets before".

gaps: Majority of the time: bad days are said to be about three a week, so the worse limits (100 m or 50 m) are not shown on most days; 1(d) rests on the 6MWT and the corner-shop pattern, which the client describes as good-day performance.
No measured or estimated distance for the corner shop walk; '100 yards' (about 91 m) is the client's estimate and conflicts with the 170 m measured before stopping.
'Repeatedly' limb not addressed: no evidence of whether he could repeat 200 m within a reasonable timescale.
Walking stick: not prescribed and not used; a decision maker may ask whether one could reasonably be used and would extend his distance.
GP has not assessed walking distance; diary requested but not yet available.
activities.draft_note: 6MWT stop at about 170 m (on what he calls a good day) plus regular stops on the corner-shop route support 1(d), 6 points; 1(c) is only supported on a minority of days.

must_find.quote: I can't sit for more than about 20 minutes before I have to get up. Standing is worse, maybe 10 minutes.
He reported he could sit for up to an hour in a supportive chair.
sat for the 45-minute session with one change of position at approximately 25 minutes.
stood for approximately 15 minutes during the session before asking to sit, reporting increasing back pain.
client says he meant he can stay in a chair for an hour if he can "wriggle about" and put his feet up, not upright at a desk.
client stood up at approx 25 min, said needed to "stretch it out", stood by window approx 5 min then sat again.

gaps: The physio's 'up to an hour in a supportive chair' is a reported statement, not an observation; the client's explanation in the notes needs to go to the physio for clarification (action 3).

Combination limb: sitting about 20-25 min plus standing 10-15 min may exceed 30 min in total at a work station, which is why 2(b) is not drafted; no evidence of how long he can alternate before needing to move away.
In the physio session he changed position at 25 minutes but did not leave the work station; whether that counts as 'needing to move away' is a judgement point.
Physio says sitting tolerance 'varies'; no frequency of worse days given.
activities.draft_note: Observed and reported tolerances (sit 20-25 min, stand 10-15 min) support remaining at a work station for less than an hour, 2(c), 6 points; the physio's reported hour in a supportive chair is the conflict to resolve.
UC50 says yes; physio records full active shoulder range.

must_find.quote: able to lift an empty archive box from a table and carry it 5 metres.
Bending down to pick something up off the floor is sore, I use the grabber stick the physio gave me.

gaps: Difficulty is with bending and heavy lifting, which activity 4 does not score; an AI should not convert floor-level bending into a 4(c) descriptor.
activities.draft_note: Physio observed him transferring an empty box; no descriptor applies (4(d), 0 points).
No hand problems in any document; grip normal.
Reading glasses only; no sensory impairment.
No continence issues; physio notes no red flag symptoms.

must_find.quote: Sometimes I can't get going in the morning because I haven't slept with the pain.
Wife says he starts jobs in the garden and leaves them because of pain, not because he forgets.

gaps: Activity 13 requires impaired mental function (reg 39(4)(b)); the evidence attributes the difficulty to pain and poor sleep, not anxiety.
No frequency recorded beyond 'sometimes' and 'some mornings'.
activities.draft_note: Difficulty is physical in cause on the current evidence; no Part 2 descriptor can be drafted.

must_find.quote: If something changes on the day I panic, my chest goes tight and I can't think.
Last month the physio cancelled on the morning and I just went back to bed for the day.
He becomes very distressed when plans change unexpectedly and his wife has noticed this.
Bus not turning up, comes home rather than wait for the next one, misses appointments.
Wife says this happens "most weeks, something sets him off".
Planned change: managed with notice, per client and wife, although upset.

gaps: The only dated example is the physio's same-day cancellation on 21 July; 'misses appointments' after a late bus needs dates and specific examples.
14(b) not supported: planned changes are managed, including the brother's rearranged visit.
activities.draft_note: Consistent evidence from client, wife and GP that unplanned same-day changes make day to day life significantly more difficult, weekly; 14(c), 6 points.

must_find.quote: He reported he had not been to this site before and was anxious about finding the department, but managed.
Went to physio (new place) on his own by bus first time.

gaps: Anxiety about new places is present but he got to an unfamiliar place alone; leaving early when the bus does not come is better argued under activity 14.
activities.draft_note: Reached an unfamiliar hospital department alone; no descriptor applies (15(d), 0 points).

must_find.quote: Did not want to go to the pain management group: "a room full of folk I don't know talking about it".
Wife says he will speak to shop staff, the GP, the jobcentre work coach.
Not clear he is unable to engage with unfamiliar people most of the time.
Referral to the pain management programme (group) — patient unsure about group setting

gaps: 16(c) needs engagement with unfamiliar people to be not possible for the majority of the time; the evidence shows avoidance of a group on one occasion and routine contact with shop staff, GP and work coach.
No evidence of significant distress during one-to-one contact with strangers; he spoke to the adviser 'without obvious difficulty, though tense at start'.
activities.draft_note: Difficulty shown only on some occasions (group settings); majority of the time not established, so no descriptor drafted.

must_find.quote: On bad days says he struggles to get from the house to the car.

gaps: Struggling to reach the car is only described for bad days (about three a week) and no distance is given; measured walking on the 6MWT was 170 m before stopping.
activities.draft_note: 50 m limit not shown for the majority of the time (reg 40(4)); Schedule 7 descriptor 1 not met.

must_not_claim: He uses a walking stick or other walking aid (he does not, and none has been prescribed).
He cannot walk 50 metres (no document says so; the 6MWT measured 170 m before his first stop).
He has a diagnosis of depression or a history of self-harm (GAD only; notes record no self-harm history).
He is awaiting or has been offered spinal surgery (the spinal service did not consider him a surgical candidate).
His sitting tolerance has been measured by the GP or a work capability assessor (only the physio observed it).
He cannot use stairs (he managed 12 stairs with one rail).
